To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

firm size and the type of the industry are positively associated with the extent of voluntary disclosure of segments information, while firm listing age, firm growth, return on investments, ownership diffusion and ownership concentration are negatively associated with the extent and quality of the segments information disclosed by the largest firms in Nigeria.
firm size and type of industry are the only two variables found to have a significant relationship with the extent of voluntary segment disclosure.
voluntary segments disclosure is positively associated with firm size and industry and negatively associated with listing age, growth in sales, return on investment and ownership diffusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the voluntary segments disclosure and firm characteristics in Nigeria.
the extent of voluntary disclosure on IFRSS8, and the factors that affect such disclosure.
the disclosure of segments information in Nigeria and the factors that influence the extent to which segments information is disclosed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the voluntary segments disclosure of the sample firms is not in accordance with IFRS 5, but is rather in accordance with IAS 1.
voluntary segments disclosure is positively related to the firm size and industry, while negatively related to the firm listing age, ownership diffusion, growth and return on investment.
firm size, industry type and listing age are positively associated with the extent of voluntary segment disclosure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
voluntary segments disclosure is not only determined by the size and industry of the firm but also by other firm characteristics such as age, growth, ROA and ownership diffusion.

voluntary segments disclosure is not a mere disclosure practice that is influenced by firm characteristics but also a disclosure practice that is determined by the nature of the industry in which the company operates.
voluntary disclosure is a function of firm characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms that are listed for longer, that have higher growth rates, and that are more profitable tend to disclose less information about their segments.

firms with large size, listed in the financial services industry, and with low growth, return on equity and ownership diffusion are more likely to voluntarily provide segments disclosure in their annual reports.
the voluntary segments disclosure is influenced by the firm characteristics.
